deliverable: MLA closure beyond the official 20 cases: Nkv>1 GQA (which NONE of the official cases exercise), explicit scale, KV tail, causal last-partial-tile, short-KV single-block, and column sharding on GQA and decode. Plus the 20-case result carried from G60/G62.

official_20_case_sweep.comparator: original cannbench_contract.Harness + npu_compare.compare_case_result, original thresholds, warm fp64 oracle cache

coverage_gap_found_in_the_official_set.statement: The official 20 cases use ONLY Nkv=1, with G in {32, 64, 128}. Computed from fixtures/mla/cases.yaml, not assumed.
coverage_gap_found_in_the_official_set.consequence: GQA with more than one KV head is completely untested by the official set, so a kernel could pass 20/20 and still mis-map heads the moment Nkv > 1. That is why the GQA cases below exist.

extended_cases.reference_agreement: every extended case is BIT-IDENTICAL to the working reference (ref=0.00e+00) and within the original golden threshold
extended_cases.explicit_scale: scaleValue 0.125 / 0.0625 / 1.0 / 0.042 all PASS; the official set only ever uses -1, so an explicit scale was untested
extended_cases.kv_tail: Skv 128/256/384/640/896 all PASS, including a single KV block
extended_cases.causal_tail: S=1 Skv=4096, S=2 Skv=2048, S=3 Skv=640, S=33 Skv=384, S=32 Skv=128 all PASS
extended_cases.sharding_on_gqa_and_decode: columnShards 2 and 4 give BIT-IDENTICAL output to unsharded on Nkv=4 GQA and on S=1 Skv=2048 decode

domain_limits_stated_as_errors.seq_kv_multiple_of_128: the KV loop advances one 128-position block per pipelined iteration; this is a real limit of the implemented SIMD packing path, not a tunable
domain_limits_stated_as_errors.group_at_least_32: the query tile is 32 or 64 rows, so G=16 is refused with MLA_BAD_TILE rather than tiled illegally
domain_limits_stated_as_errors.d_rope_equals_64: the rope GEMM is one 64-wide panel
domain_limits_stated_as_errors.d_nope_multiple_of_64: the nope GEMM accumulates in 64-wide panels
domain_limits_stated_as_errors.note: Each is refused LOUDLY. The alternative -- silently tiling an unsupported shape -- would return plausible wrong numbers.

v_equals_k_nope_is_a_value_contract.statement: The kernel reads the K_nope tile and uses it as V. No assumption is made about pointer aliasing, and the v argument is deliberately not read.
v_equals_k_nope_is_a_value_contract.why_it_is_safe: V_j == K_nope_j is the operator value contract, and K_nope is already resident when PV runs, so re-reading it would double GM traffic for no gain.
v_equals_k_nope_is_a_value_contract.lifetime: the K_nope slot is not released until the final PV completes

my_own_test_bugs_recorded: Six GQA cases first reported failure with MLA_KV_NOT_MULTIPLE_OF_128. Cause: MY test passed Skv=64, which is not a multiple of 128. The kernel was right to refuse it and the error message named the reason; I had written inputs outside the stated domain.
An earlier GQA batch failed with MLA_BAD_TILE because I chose G=16, below the 32-row query tile. Also my input, also correctly refused.
Both classes were fixed by computing the legal domain from cases.yaml and the kernel own checks rather than inventing shapes.
not_claimed: No performance claim. No cycle timings, no comparison against any baseline.
The extended cases do NOT substitute for the official 20; they complement it.
Uneven column-shard widths are unsupported by design and not assessed.
Numerical agreement is not a formal proof over all inputs, and no physical synchronisation equivalence is asserted.
